title: Python Instance Attributes, Class Attributes and Properties
learningObjectives: Explain the core concepts of Python Instance Attributes, Class Attributes and Properties.
Choose an appropriate object-oriented design for a small Python problem.
Trace object state and method calls accurately.
Apply Python class features with correct method and attribute behavior.
Recognize design trade-offs, edge cases and maintainability concerns.

understand.concept: Instance attributes belong to individual objects; class attributes live on the class and may be shared. An instance assignment can shadow a class attribute. Properties expose method-backed behavior through attribute syntax and can validate assignments using a setter.
understand.whyItMatters: Choosing the right attribute scope prevents accidental shared state, while properties preserve a clean public interface and enforce invariants.
understand.analogy: A class attribute is a common notice posted for all members; an instance attribute is a personal note. A property is a controlled counter window that checks each update.
understand.summary: Python Instance Attributes, Class Attributes and Properties introduces a focused part of Python's object model and its practical use.

explain.narrative: Study the concept, trace the receiver and state for each operation, then run the examples. Pay attention to Python's conventions and documented protocol behavior rather than assuming that class syntax provides strict access control.

examples.title: Read a class attribute
examples.code:
class Plan:
    currency = 'INR'
a, b = Plan(), Plan()
print(a.currency, b.currency)
examples.explanation: Both instances resolve the same class-level value.

examples.title: Shadow a class attribute
examples.code:
class Plan:
    tier = 'basic'
a, b = Plan(), Plan()
a.tier = 'pro'
print(a.tier, b.tier)
examples.explanation: An instance assignment creates an instance attribute that shadows the class attribute.

examples.title: Use a property getter
examples.explanation: A property computes a value while being accessed like an attribute.

examples.title: Validate with a property setter
examples.explanation: A setter centralizes validation whenever the public attribute is assigned.

examples.title: Inspect class and instance dictionaries
examples.code:
class Item:
    group = 'A'
x = Item()
x.code = 7
print(x.__dict__, Item.__dict__['group'])
examples.explanation: An instance dictionary contains its instance attributes; class attributes are stored on the class.

practise.guidedTask: Build a small program that demonstrates python instance attributes, class attributes and properties. Write down the object types, relevant attributes, method calls and expected state changes before running it.
practise.independentTask: Extend the example into a small domain model of your choice. Add validation, clear method names, boundary tests and a short explanation of why your design uses classes rather than simpler functions or data structures.
hints: Identify which object owns each piece of state.
Trace the first argument supplied to every bound method.
Prefer explicit invariants and small public interfaces.
Test at least one boundary or unsupported input.
Use composition when it models the relationship more accurately than inheritance.
practise.challenge: Refactor the model into a testable design with clear responsibilities, documented public behavior and tests for normal, boundary and invalid cases.
validationCriteria: All five examples execute on the supported Python version and match their outputs.
The implementation follows Python's documented class and special-method semantics.
State changes are scoped to the intended object or class.
Unsupported inputs produce a deliberate result or a clear exception.
The design avoids unnecessary inheritance, shared mutable defaults and misleading private-access claims.

questions.prompt: Where is an instance attribute stored by default?
questions.explanation: Instance attributes usually live in the instance namespace.

questions.prompt: What happens when an instance assigns a class attribute name?
questions.answer: It can shadow the class attribute
options: It can shadow the class attribute
It converts it to a property
questions.explanation: An instance-level value takes precedence during attribute lookup.
Properties expose getter behavior through attribute syntax.

questions.prompt: What is a property setter useful for?
questions.explanation: A setter can enforce invariants on assignment.

questions.prompt: Are class attributes automatically copied into each instance dictionary?
questions.explanation: Instances resolve class attributes through lookup without copying them into __dict__.
